sources.supports: getVersion, getStatuses, getPriorities, getResultFields, getCaseFields and getCaseTypes each take no argument and issue one GET to their own endpoint with no path segment, query or body, parsing the reply with the matching schema. getDynamicFilterFields and getTemplates validate the project identifier with validateId and place it as the only path segment. None of them consults another endpoint first, so no call here triggers a version or capability request of its own.

StatusSchema requires id, name, label, the three numeric colour fields color_dark, color_medium and color_bright, and the booleans is_system, is_untested and is_final. PrioritySchema requires id, name, short_name, is_default and priority. CaseTypeSchema and TemplateSchema each require id, name and is_default and admit a nullish i18n_custom_id. DynamicFilterFieldSchema requires type_id, system_name and label and admits nullish options and sub_filters strings, its comment describing the two as mutually endpoint-dependent. TestRailVersionSchema requires a version string and its comment dates the endpoint to TestRail 10.6. Every object is passthrough, so unmodelled keys survive parsing.

The 10.6.1 release notes announce get_version as a new endpoint, GET index.php?/api/v2/get_version, returning the current TestRail version, for example {"version": "10.6.0.1041"}, and requiring an active, authenticated session. The endpoint has no page in TestRail's API reference section.

input_policy.notes: The endpoint takes nothing: the release notes document no parameter and the driver sends none, so every field is refused. The tool is the only way this server ever reaches the endpoint: no startup step, capability probe or other tool asks for the version, and no tool is offered or withheld by its answer.

outer_result.notes: The version record is returned as the driver received it, including any field beside version that a server adds. Entity-field drift is advisory.

requirements.description: Reject unknown top-level fields before driver invocation rather than forwarding or discarding them.
Call the driver with no arguments at all, and send no path segment, query or body.
